answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Lockstep Rule. Each identity commits an unpredictable-path schedule per epoch; across epochs, its movement must echo its prior trajectory within tolerance, or rewards freeze. Clones can't cheaply match a target's path because divergence forces a costly re-registration and a fresh observation period. An attacker must run full-cost agents through many epochs, letting targets wander and diverge on a reef of decoy routes, multiplying the number of sustained behaviors needed.
